summary: YBCO coplanar waveguide cavities integrated with helium-ion-generated Josephson junctions exhibit GHz-range flux tunability via periodic SQUID oscillations overlaid with Fraunhofer-like single-junction modulation due to out-of-plane junction barriers. The devices operate up to 14 K with junction-induced quality factors of $Q_{J0} \sim 200$–$700$, enabling independent tuning of resonance frequency and flux responsivity.
motivation: High-temperature superconductors like YBCO can operate in elevated temperatures and large magnetic fields inaccessible to aluminum, but integrating tunable Josephson inductances has proven difficult; helium-ion-generated barrier junctions offer flexible dose-dependent control of critical currents ($I_c$ varied over three orders of magnitude via line dose $D_\ell$).
method: Three quarter-wave CPW cavities on 50 nm M-type YBCO/MgO were patterned, pre-characterized at 4.2 K to obtain $Q_{\mathrm{int},c} \sim 3000$, then integrated with He-FIB SQUIDs by irradiating at $D_{\mathrm{cav}} = 1100$ ions/nm to create critical currents $I_0 \sim 1.5$–$2.8$ µA; resonance and loss factors were extracted from $S_{21}$ measurements versus bias flux and temperature (2.1–14 K).
result: Cavity R1 showed tuning range $\gtrsim 310$ MHz with $\partial\omega_0/\partial\Phi_b \approx 2\pi \times 5$ GHz$\,\Phi_0^{-1}$, R3 reached $\gtrsim 1$ GHz with $\partial\omega_0/\partial\Phi_b \approx 2\pi \times 24$ GHz$\,\Phi_0^{-1}$; Fraunhofer envelope appeared at $\pm 53\,\Phi_0$ (0.53 mT) allowing frequency tuning at flux sweetspots with zero first-order field noise sensitivity; junction resistance extracted as $R_J \approx 100$ Ω matches dc voltage-state values, enabling loss prediction via $1/Q_{J0} \propto I_0^{-2}$.
